answer: Latency Summit Quorum: each new identity must publish its first 64 outbound messages, and peers check that inter-message gaps follow a skewed distribution with a Falcon-tight median (a timing fingerprint). Violators get throttled to one request per Violet interval, effectively starving flood-spawned clones. Enforcement is statistical, not binary, so an attacker must run each clone through real-time pacing for hours, paying compute and wall-clock delay per identity rather than a one-off fee.
